profiles.summary: Wheat favours structured loam or clay loam with drainage and moisture retention.
profiles.texture: Loam, light loam or clay loam; an alluvial label alone does not identify texture.
profiles.drainage: Check drainage and soil structure; a heavy soil needs an open, aerated structure.
profiles.scope: General wheat guidance; not a Chhapra field trial.

profiles.summary: Rice is grown on riverine alluvium and several other soils; clay-rich soils retain water well.
profiles.texture: Clay or clay loam with organic matter is preferred for water retention.
profiles.drainage: Manage water retention for the rice establishment system; problem soils also need a drainage plan.
profiles.scope: General preferred range, not the full rice tolerance range or a Bihar prescription.

profiles.summary: Maize requires fertile soil that drains freely.
profiles.texture: Assess fertility and drainage from a field soil test and inspection.
profiles.drainage: Use well-drained soil; review standing water before irrigation.
profiles.scope: General optimum pH; source reports a wider range of 5.5–8.0. Confirm Bihar management locally.

profiles.summary: Mustard generally performs best on medium to heavy loam.
profiles.texture: Medium or heavy loam; requirements vary between rapeseed-mustard species.
profiles.drainage: Check drainage with the local crop advisory before planting.
profiles.source: Rajasthan Agriculture Competitiveness Project · Mustard value chain
profiles.scope: Rajasthan reference; not a Bihar fertilizer or variety recommendation.

profiles.summary: Bengal gram prefers well-drained soils with medium fertility.
profiles.drainage: Inspect drainage before sowing; the reference specifies well-drained conditions.
profiles.source: Government of India · NFSM package of practices
profiles.scope: General crop guidance; soil-test advice takes precedence.

bihar.note: Bihar has extensive alluvial soils. ICAR identifies drainage, salinity/alkalinity and sulphur, boron and zinc deficiencies as regional constraints. These are testing priorities, not confirmed problems in your field.

soilTest.note: Request pH, EC, organic carbon, available nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium, sulphur, zinc and boron on the soil report. Use the laboratory's crop-specific recommendation for nutrient quantities and amendment rates.
soilTest.source: Government of India · Soil Health Card teacher manual
